Where mixed-four-sources sits on the map

12,000 records in 4 datasets; en 99%, nl under 0.1%, no under 0.1% and 24 more, measured against atlas-v2. This sits between a specialist set and a general mixture: several areas, with most of the weight in a few of them.

Coverage

Reach 132.9 / 296 subregions, summing min(1, density) over each; records were found in 274

Subject areas

One block per subject area your data reached, the areas holding most of your records first. Inside each, subregions are listed densest first. Record counts are estimates when only part of your data was checked.

no reach as common as on the map over-represented, up to 87×

Density is your share of a subregion against the reference corpus's share of the same one: 1.0× matches the map. 2× is twice as common as on the map; 0 means none was found in the sample.

Reach sums min(1, density) over an area's subregions, so parity is a full score and over-representation does not add more. 15 / 16 means the sum falls one short of the area’s subregions: extra records in one subregion do not fill a gap in another.

Names describe the reference text, not your records. The records quoted beside them are your own, and are what the names stand for here.
